page: Microsoft Azure L2as_v4 is an entry-level storage-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core via multithreading, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, giving an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Compute instructions include AVX-512 support with VNNI and BF16 extensions, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic operations. The VM includes 480 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and zero bundled GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations highlight clear performance distinctions stemming from the core configuration. Single-core throughput is competitive, with stress-ng single-core execution reaching 3077.27 and Geekbench single-core hitting 2034.0, both placing in the upper quartile. Conversely, aggregate multithreaded capacity is constrained by the two-vCPU ceiling, as reflected by a PassMark CPU score of 3830.78 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2584.0. Large-block memory bandwidth tests show 35.99 GB/sec read and 27.68 GB/sec write throughput, while Redis SET performance registers at 3.18 million operations per second.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the L2as_v4 offers an economical entry point into storage-dense computing without requiring provisioning of large multi-core nodes. The direct pairing of 480 GB local NVMe storage with a generous 8.0 GB per vCPU memory balance allows data-intensive applications to minimize external drive attachments. However, users face a throughput tradeoff: workloads demanding parallel processing or intensive multi-client database operations will face saturation quickly on the single underlying physical core.

This server type is primarily suited for local-storage cache layers, lightweight database replicas, log ingestion nodes, and modest web services requiring fast NVMe scratch storage. Applications relying heavily on single-thread efficiency coupled with fast local disk operations represent the optimal operational profile.
description: Microsoft Azure L2as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine delivering 2 dedicated vCPUs across a single physical AMD EPYC 9V74 core clocked at 3.7 GHz. Equipped with 16.0 GB of memory and 480 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, it offers a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU without bundled GPU acceleration. The instance exhibits strong single-core performance, achieving high percentiles in Geekbench and stress-ng tests, alongside support for AVX-512 extensions and hardware cryptography. However, total compute throughput remains constrained by its two-vCPU ceiling, limiting high-concurrency scalability. The hardware configuration emphasizes localized fast storage paired with substantial memory capacity relative to compute capacity. As a result, the L2as_v4 functions effectively for small caching tiers, log ingestion agents, lightweight transactional databases, and localized data processing tasks that benefit from dedicated NVMe read and write performance rather than heavy parallel computation.
